items.source: When I first tried to learn CUDA for deep learning, I often found myself missing the connective tissue between ideas. I could find explanations of CUDA mechanics, and I could find examples of sophisticated kernels, but I still had to work out how the pieces lined up: how threads map to tensors, how memory access patterns become performance problems, how reductions show up inside ordinary model operations, and why attention changes the shape of the whole optimization problem.
items.translated: 当我第一次尝试学习CUDA进行深度学习时，我经常发现自己缺少想法之间的结缔组织。我可以找到CUDA机制的解释，我可以找到复杂内核的例子，但我仍然需要弄清楚这些部分是如何排列的：线程如何映射到张量，记忆访问模式如何成为性能问题，在普通模型操作中如何减少，以及为什么注意力会改变整个最佳化问题的形状。

items.source: I think that perspective matters. An expert who has lived in this world for a decade can forget which steps are nonobvious at the beginning. I tried to keep those steps visible: what the GPU is doing, why the code is shaped the way it is, where the profiler is pointing, and how a small kernel-level choice connects to the larger deep learning workload.
items.translated: 我认为这种观点很重要。一个在这个世界上生活了十年的专家可能会忘记哪些步骤在开始时是不明显的。我试图保持这些步骤的可见性：GPU在做什么，为什么代码是这样塑造的，分析器指向哪里，以及一个小的内核级选择如何连接到更大的深度学习工作负载。
